tegnsætning.explanation: "Tegnsætning" means "punctuation". It is built from "et tegn" (a mark) and "at sætte" (to put).

teknisk.explanation: "Teknisk" means "technical". To say "technically speaking", use "teknisk set": "Teknisk set er det muligt" (Technically speaking, it is possible).

temmelig.explanation: "Temmelig" means "rather". To say how sure you are, put it before "sikker" (sure): "Jeg er temmelig sikker" (I am rather sure).

tennis.explanation: "Tennis" means "tennis". It goes with the verb "at spille" (to play): "Vi spiller tennis hver søndag" (We play tennis every Sunday).

teoretisk.explanation: "Teoretisk" means "theoretical". To say "in theory", use "teoretisk set": "Teoretisk set kan det lade sig gøre" (Theoretically, it can be done).

terapi.explanation: "Terapi" means "a therapy". The person who gives it is "en terapeut" (a therapist).

ternet.explanation: "Ternet" means "checkered". To say squared paper, use "ternet papir" (squared paper).

terrorisme.explanation: "Terrorisme" means "terrorism". The ending "-isme" is the same as English "-ism", as in "kapitalisme" (capitalism).

ti.explanation: "Ti" means "ten", said like "tee". Do not mix it up with "tid" (time), which ends in "d": "Jeg har ikke tid" (I do not have time).

tidevand.explanation: "Et tidevand" means "a tide". It is built from "tid" (time) and "vand" (water). The high point is "højvande" (high tide), and the low point is "lavvande" (low tide).

tidlig.explanation: "Tidlig" means "early". To say you do something early, use "tidligt" (early) instead: "Jeg står tidligt op" (I get up early).

tidligere.explanation: "Tidligere" means "earlier". To say something happened before now, use it after the verb: "Vi sås tidligere" (We met earlier). To name a past role, put it before the role to mean "former": "en tidligere elev" (a former student).

tidligt.explanation: "Tidligt" means "early". To say you do something early, put it after the verb: "Vi kom tidligt" (We came early). To describe a thing as early, use "tidlig" (early) instead: "en tidlig morgen" (an early morning).

tidskrævende.explanation: "Tidskrævende" means "time-consuming". It is built from "tid" (time) and "krævende" (demanding).

tidspres.explanation: "Et tidspres" means "a time pressure". It is built from "tid" (time) and "et pres" (a pressure).

tidssvarende.explanation: "Tidssvarende" means "up-to-date". It is built from "en tid" (a time) and "svarende" (matching). To say information is current, use "opdateret" (updated): "Siden er opdateret" (The page is updated).

tiende.explanation: "Tiende" means "tenth". To say a date, use "den tiende juni" (the tenth of June), which is written "10. juni" with a dot after the number.

til.explanation: "Til" means "to". To say where you are going, put it before the place: "Toget kører til København" (The train goes to Copenhagen). To say who something is for, it means "for": "Gaven er til dig" (The gift is for you). To say what a meal is for, use "til morgenmad" (for breakfast). To say when at a holiday, use "til jul" (at Christmas).

til fælles.explanation: "Til fælles" means "in common". It goes with "at have" (to have): "at have noget til fælles" (to have something in common).

til gengæld.explanation: "Til gengæld" means "on the other hand". To add a good side to something bad, use it after "men" (but): "Huset er lille, men til gengæld er det billigt" (The house is small, but on the other hand it is cheap). It also means "in return": "Jeg laver mad, og til gengæld tager du opvasken" (I cook, and in return you do the dishes).

til højre.explanation: "Til højre" means "to the right". To give a direction, say: "Vi skal køre til højre ved bageren" (We have to turn right at the bakery). To say where something is, say: "Kaffen står til højre" (The coffee is on the right).

til sidst.explanation: "Til sidst" means "finally / in the end". Literally, it is "to last", since "sidst" means "last". To say what happened after everything else, use it at the start: "Til sidst blev det mørkt" (In the end it got dark).

til tiden.explanation: "Til tiden" means "on time". Literally, it is "to the time". To tell someone to arrive on time, use it with "at komme" (to come): "Kom til tiden!" (Come on time!).

til venstre.explanation: "Til venstre" means "to the left". To give a direction, say: "Drej til venstre" (Turn left). To say where something is, say: "Bordet står til venstre" (The table is on the left).

tilbage.explanation: "Tilbage" means "back". To say someone returns, put it after the verb: "Hun går tilbage" (She goes back). It also means "left over": "Der er to tilbage" (There are two left). For the back of your body, use "en ryg" (a back) instead: "Jeg har ondt i ryggen" (My back hurts).
